evidence.claim: Booking Holdings disclosed that approximately 89% of 2025, 2024, and 2023 revenue related to online accommodation reservation services, with the majority of merchant revenue and substantially all agency revenue from Booking.com's accommodation reservations.

Booking Holdings' 2025 10-K states that the company is expanding merchant service offerings to provide more payment options to travelers and travel service providers and to support its Connected Trip strategy.

Sabre's 2024 annual report described Travel Solutions distribution revenue from bookings through its GDS and partner channels, generally paid by travel suppliers, and also disclosed Hospitality Solutions metrics tied to SynXis CRS transaction volumes before the later divestiture.

Sabre's 2025 annual report notes that, after the 2025 disposition of Hospitality Solutions, the company reports as one business segment and that the buyer purchased an extensive suite of software solutions for hoteliers.
Global Business Travel Group operates American Express Global Business Travel as a software and services company for corporate travel, expense, and meetings and events.
evidence.source_title: Global Business Travel Group SEC Filings and Company Overview

evidence.claim: Public annual-report summaries describe GBTG's business as a marketplace and AI-powered software/services platform, supporting the view that the company is a corporate-travel distribution layer rather than a hotel or airline capacity owner.
evidence.source_title: Global Business Travel Group, Inc. 2025 Annual Report: Business Overview, Marketplace, AI-Powered Solutions & Risk Factors

evidence.claim: Travelzoo reported Q1 2025 revenue of $23.1 million, operating profit of $3.7 million, cash flow from operations of $3.3 million, and described revenue as advertising revenues, commissions, and membership fees.
Travelzoo's CEO stated that the company would leverage its global reach, trusted brand, and relationships with top travel suppliers to negotiate Club Offers for Club Members.
As of June 9, 2026, Sabre's market capitalization was approximately $658 million, placing it in the preferred small-cap discovery range but below $1 billion.
As of June 9, 2026, Global Business Travel Group's market capitalization was approximately $4.86 billion, placing it in the preferred mid-cap discovery range.
As of June 9, 2026, Travelzoo's market capitalization was approximately $110 million, so it is below the preferred $300 million floor and should be treated as a speculative exception.

memory_update.text: BKNG should remain the reference leader for the travel marketplace tollbooth node, but should not crowd out the discovery lane in later Serenity passes.
SABR is the most direct under-$1B US-listed travel distribution infrastructure candidate, but the hotel-connectivity thesis must be adjusted for the 2025 Hospitality Solutions sale.
GBTG maps to a corporate-travel distribution tollbooth rather than consumer OTA exposure; later work should test retention, SME growth, and supplier-content economics.
TZOO is a below-$300M speculative exception with possible curated-demand/supplier-relationship value, but it needs unusually strict verification of recurring membership quality and cash generation.
US-listed hotel connectivity/channel-management pure plays are scarce; many cleaner hotel CRS/channel-manager assets appear private, foreign-listed, or embedded inside larger companies.

node: Travel marketplace and hotel distribution tollbooths
summary: Layer 1B expands the node from obvious OTAs into smaller travel-distribution tollbooths: GDS distribution, corporate-travel marketplaces, curated travel-deal demand aggregation, and hotel/experience marketplace layers. Booking Holdings is retained only as the reference leader/context anchor. The more relevant discovery candidates are Sabre, Global Business Travel Group, and Travelzoo; each has plausible direct or second-order exposure to travel demand through supplier connectivity, customer relationships, or transaction/advertising/subscription monetization, but each requires later-layer verification of take rate durability, supplier dependence, balance-sheet risk, and whether traffic/demand converts without excessive marketing spend.
